questions.q: Why are there so many kinds of plants and animals?
questions.a: Each kind is adapted to its own food, climate and home - nature supports great variety.

questions.q: Name two very different living things around you.
questions.a: A tiny ant and a huge banyan tree - both are living with different designs.

questions.q: What makes each organism suited to its place?
questions.a: Its body features and habits - fins for fish, wings for birds.

questions.q: On what features can we group living things?
questions.a: Where they live, what they eat, body coverings, and how they move or grow.

questions.q: Group a rose plant, cow and crow in any way you like.
questions.a: By movement: cow and crow move about, rose is fixed. By food: cow and rose make/eat plants, crow eats both.

questions.q: Why is grouping (classification) useful in science?
questions.a: It makes studying many things easy by putting similar ones together.

questions.q: What is a habitat? Give two examples.
questions.a: The place where an organism lives with air, water and food - pond, forest, desert.

questions.q: Name two animals of the desert and their adaptation.
questions.a: Camel (stores fat, needs little water) and desert rat (burrows by day).

questions.q: Why can a fish not live on land?
questions.a: It breathes through gills that take oxygen only from water.
Written records can be compared, checked and used to draw conclusions.

questions.q: Name two ways of recording observations.
questions.a: A science diary with drawings, and tables of measurements.
Careful use of senses, exact measurements, and honest notes without guessing.
